answer.evidence: radon/metrics.py:150-157 defines mi_rank(score) as chr(65 + (9 - score >= 0) + (19 - score >= 0)). That gives A for score > 19, B for 9 < score <= 19, and C for score <= 9. The boundary values 9 and 19 are inclusive on the lower grade, which matches the docstring. The expression relies on bool-to-int arithmetic, so it needs boundary tests at 9, 9.01, 19 and 19.01. Reviewing radon/visitors.py and radon/raw.py is also needed. They produce the inputs to the maintainability index (the complexity and LOC/comment counts that mi_visit consumes), and errors there would shift scores across the 9 and 19 cut points. The review should confirm that the float and rounding behaviour of those inputs does not change which side of a threshold a score lands on.
